title: Koroye
summary: Portfolio platform for Keniye Koroye, an industrial designer, researcher, product strategist, and innovation leader.
shortDescription: A digital platform showcasing multidisciplinary design, research, and innovation work.

overview: A digital platform for industrial designer, researcher, and product strategist Keniye Koroye.
The objective was to create a portfolio that reflected multidisciplinary work across design, innovation, and research.
The project needed to feel editorial and personal while still giving structure to a broad body of work.
contribution: Built the frontend with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Framer Motion.
Structured the content architecture around design, research, strategy, and innovation work.
Implemented responsive editorial layouts that support multiple types of multidisciplinary work.
Used strong typography and modular sections to keep the portfolio clear and engaging.
challenges: The website needed to present several disciplines without overwhelming visitors.
Research, industrial design, strategy, and innovation all needed equal importance.
The content architecture had to support different types of work without flattening them into one generic portfolio format.
The visual presentation needed to feel distinctive while keeping navigation and reading flow simple.
approach: Used strong typography and visual hierarchy to give the portfolio a more editorial feel.
Created modular content sections that could support different kinds of multidisciplinary work.
Built responsive layouts that keep research, product strategy, industrial design, and innovation content easy to browse.
Structured the interface so the platform could feel personal without becoming hard to navigate.
outcome: The platform showcases multidisciplinary work through a clear and engaging experience.
The final website gives Keniye Koroye a stronger digital platform for presenting design, research, strategy, and innovation work.
The experience balances personality and structure, making the portfolio feel more memorable while keeping the work accessible.
caseStudy.pullQuote: The experience had to give equal weight to design, research, strategy, and innovation.
